chunks: Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Silver for silver must be equal, and gold for gold must be equal. There must be neither an increase nor a delay. The one who gives extra and the one who seeks extra are in the Fire.

key_terms.الذَّهَبُ: gold as a ribawi item in exchange
key_terms.الزَّائِدُ: the one who gives an unlawful excess
key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, meaning punishment in the Hereafter
key_terms.الْفِضَّةُ: silver as a ribawi item in exchange
key_terms.الْمُسْتَزِيدُ: the one who seeks or takes an unlawful excess
key_terms.زِيَادَةٌ: any excess added in the exchange
key_terms.مِثْلٌ بِمِثْلٍ: equal in amount, like for like

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging gold for gold or silver for silver in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling that when silver is exchanged for silver, or gold for gold, the exchange must be equal and immediate. It condemns both giving and taking an unlawful excess in such transactions, warning of punishment in the Fire.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4037 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"Silver for silver must be equal, and gold for gold must be equal, there should be neither an increase nor a delay. The one who gives extra and the one who demands extra will be in the Fire."
